subject: Request: Uptime & Latency Matrix Exception for Mosaic Health (high-touch)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Uptime & Latency Matrix Exception for Mosaic Health (high-touch)

Team — quick heads up: Mosaic Health (large regional payer) just pushed a firm procurement ask: they want a written availability/latency matrix baked into the SOW and signed by legal + ops. They are asking for 99.995% monthly uptime and p95 inference latency <= 85ms for their burst profile, with penalty language.

Background: account is on Dedicated Reserved (2x A100 pools) with burst to our hosted capacity. They are at pilot -> production ramp and procurement wants the higher tier SLA as a condition of the multi-year deal (DEAL-4391).

Ask: can Product/Runtime approve a scoped carveout for this account? Specifically we need to confirm:
- whether we can commit a p95 <= 85ms for their traffic shape (seq avg 512 tokens, 3 concurrent services)
- what the operational pre-reqs are (dedicated hot standby, canary rollout window, runbook)
- what limits/penalties we can accept without opening a precedent risk

Attaching the procurement request and their proposed SLA matrix for context. I want a short internal summary + redlines we can send to Procurement by Friday EOD.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[attachment: mosaic-procurement-SLA-request.pdf (PDF)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-10T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Uptime & Latency Matrix Exception for Mosaic Health (high-touch)

Thanks Vanessa — reading through the PDF. Short answer: 85ms p95 is aggressive but may be achievable with Dedicated + optimized routing and a KV/prefix cache for common prompts. A few clarifying points I need before we commit anything:

1) Traffic profile — can we get a sample 48-72 hour trace (qps distribution, seq length histogram)? If their pattern has high concurrency peaks we need to size GPU pools and pre-warm.
2) Model variant — which model are they routing to? Quantized v1.2 or fp16? Latency changes substantially.
3) Fallback policy — do we allow a slightly higher-latency fallback model in the event of capacity exhaustion?

Operational asks that would make 85ms realistic:
- Dedicated hot standby with single-tenant pre-warmed instances (additional reserve cost)
- Canary rollout with 2-week burn-in and latency SLO measurement window
- Explicit maintenance windows + expedited change freeze during business hours

I can draft a proposed carveout with conditional language (e.g., \"Commitment applies when account uses dedicated pre-warmed capacity and follows runbook X; otherwise standard SLA applies\").

Will loop in Runtime (Laura) and Ops (Marcus) for capacity confirmation.

— Rishi
Head of Product, Serving Runtime

From: Jane Douglas <jane.douglas@mosaichealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, procurement@mosaichealth.com
Date: 2027-10-11T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mosaic SLA ask — clarifications

Vanessa — thanks for the quick response. A couple clarifications from our side:
- We expect production to start Nov 1 and will route all clinical inference through the dedicated route (no public endpoints).
- Expected steady-state qps ~180 (peak 400) with most requests under 800 tokens.
- Model: we require the ensemble you provided in your architecture doc (fp16 for primary; quantized fallback for cost-optimized loads).

Procurement attached our standard SLA appendix; we'd appreciate Redwood's counter with any conditional language but this SLA is a gating item.

Jane
Director, Digital Health Partnerships
Mosaic Health
[attachment: mosaic-sla-template-v3.pdf (PDF)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-12T11:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Uptime & Latency Matrix Exception for Mosaic Health (high-touch)

Vanessa / Rishi — read both attachments. Quick technical summary:
- Given their qps and token distribution, p95 <= 85ms is feasible only if the primary path runs on pre-warmed dedicated instances with: single-tenant scheduling, pinned kernel optimizations, and KV prefix cache enabled.
- If they insist on fp16 primary and quantized fallback, we need an A/B fallback gating strategy; quantized fallback improves cost but adds ~30-45ms tail latency in our current kernels.
- We can commit to the uptime figure for Dedicated pools provided we define a clear operational boundary: any third-party network outage or scheduled maintenance declared with 48h notice is excluded.

Operational requirements I'd include in the carveout:
1) Dedicated hot standby with automated failover testing weekly (reporting required)
2) Canary rollout window: 14 calendar days with explicit rollback criteria
3) Monthly SLA review and a jointly maintained incident runbook (Ops + Customer)
4) Capacity scaling trigger thresholds and a cost-sharing clause for pre-warm capacity beyond baseline

I'll attach a short tech appendix for the legal team to reference.

— Laura
Principal Runtime Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: runtime-appendix-mosaic.pdf (PDF)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-13T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Request: Uptime & Latency Matrix Exception for Mosaic Health (high-touch) — Legal / Finance check

Forwarding procurement's SLA appendix and the internal tech note. Legal asked finance for guidance on penalty exposure. Two quick points from my side:
- We should avoid open-ended financial penalties tied to fractional uptime numbers. Propose defined credit cap (e.g., max 10% of monthly invoice) and a step-down penalty (not continuous).
- For architecture-mandated costs (pre-warm hot standby), propose a separate monthly surcharge line item rather than embedding into the base price — this keeps the core unit economics transparent.

Marcus, can you run a cost delta for maintaining the requested dedicated hot-standby for their projected qps (180 steady / 400 peak)? I need ballpark delta to propose to finance.

Thanks — Priyom
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-14T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Uptime & Latency Matrix Exception for Mosaic Health (high-touch)

All — ran the numbers with Ops. Summary & proposed go/no-go conditions: 

1) Cost: an additional reserved hot-standby (1.2x baseline) and pre-warm buffer will add ~22% to the monthly Dedicated cost for this account. We can put that as a separate line item and cap the surcharge with a 12‑month commitment.
2) Latency: if the customer agrees to the operational pre-reqs Laura outlined (pre-warmed single-tenant, KV cache, canary burn-in), we will instrument p95 as part of the rollout and commit to a conditional p95 <= 85ms. This will be in the SLA as: 
   \"Commitment applies only when account is on dedicated pre-warmed capacity, follows the jointly maintained runbook, and uses primary fp16 model routing. Outages due to third-party network or customer-side misconfiguration are excluded.\"
3) Penalties: Legal/Finance recommend a credit schedule (tiered credits up to 10% monthly invoice) and a quarterly review clause rather than automatic financial escalation.

Decision: recommend approval to accept the carveout with the above conditional language and a clearly defined surcharge. Marcus will prepare a short operational annex (runbook + monitoring hooks) to attach to the SOW.

Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
[attachment: ops-cost-breakdown-mosaic.xlsx (XLSX)]
